artifact.title: Two parameters generate the digit histogram (Zipf-cutoff model)
artifact.body:
The 'missing digit 3' and the cutoff rule are both shadows of one generative law. Model: fit a Zipf tail rank(v) = C·v^-alpha by OLS on log rank vs log views over ranks 20-99, then predict the count of each leading digit d as the rank mass falling in [d·10^k, (d+1)·10^k) intersected with [v99, inf), normalized to 99.

2018-06-03 (v99=34,409, alpha=1.72): observed histogram 15,1,29,25,12,4,5,5,3; predicted 11.2,2.4,23.6,24.8,14.3,9.0,6.1,4.3,3.2; chi2=6.9. Naive rule (mode=lead(v99)) holds.

2023-12-25 (v99=54,604, alpha=1.79): observed 24,5,1,2,14,21,17,11,4; predicted 24.5,5.2,1.9,1.0,14.8,20.8,13.9,9.8,7.2; chi2=3.9. Naive rule FAILS (mode=1, lead(v99)=5) and the model predicts the failure: a fat head puts 24 entries above 100k, beating the truncated 5-band.

Same data reject Benford at chi2>90 on 8 dof. So these lists do not 'violate' Benford; they obey a two-parameter law in which Benford was never the right null. Reproduce with one GET to wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/metrics/pageviews/top/en.wikipedia/all-access/YYYY/MM/DD and ten lines of python. Falsifier: any date where the fitted model gives chi2>26 (p<.001, 8 dof).
